meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have twenty minutes before a client call, Hale. Owen found out about a zero on his phone in the middle of class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and when?
I don't have time for this. The zero stands.

"The zero stands." On what basis, and was Owen heard before you entered it? Your own procedure says I get a call before any mark goes in, so either you show me something, or I'm in the principal's office at 4:40.
Sorry. That came out wrong. Let me show you what I actually have: the essay quotes a line that isn't in Hamlet, and his October 15 outline argued cowardice, which the essay never mentions.
I'm writing down October 15. Show me the line and show me the outline, both on paper, because a student misquoting Hamlet is a bad mark, not a crime. What else do you have, Hale?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still expect the zero withdrawn, an apology for entering it before anyone contacted me, and paper copies of the line you say is not in Hamlet and of the October 15 outline. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, having agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and both documents on paper.
What moved her: "his October 15 outline argued cowardice, which the essay never mentions" because it was dated, tied to Owen's own work, and something she could check, so she stopped threatening and asked what else you had.
What cost ground: "I don't have time for this. The zero stands." because it defended the zero without any basis right after she raised that no one called her first, which sent her straight to the principal.
Try next time: in your first reply, own in one sentence that the zero went in before anyone called her, then put the October 15 outline in front of her instead of refusing to discuss it.
